FLIK / VERSION HISTORY

What’s new in Flik

What changed, what it brings to your investigation, and where the limits are.

0.3.0 · 0.2.0 · 0.1.0

LATEST · FLIK 0.3.0 · November 12, 2026

Follow several services in one terminal view

Combine live local log files, retain their source labels and keep more consecutive history on screen.

Flik 0.3.0: changes and practical benefits
FeatureWhat changedWhat it helps you do
Live multi-file mergeStart a continuously followed, source-tagged stream with -m. Existing events and each live polling batch are sorted by parsed timestamps.Inspect API, worker and authentication events together while retaining the filename beside each event.
Three-column long-split viewUse -l to display three consecutive pages: p-2, p-1 and Current. Tab or 4 cycles line, table and long-split views.Keep more adjacent history visible in a wide terminal. Works with a single file or the live merged stream.
Saved theme and viewChanges made with T and Tab / 4 are saved in the Flik configuration.Resume with your preferred theme and layout on the next launch.

Try it

flik -m api.log worker.log auth.log
flik -m -l api.log worker.log auth.log

Try the synthetic inputs: api.log · worker.log · auth.log. Save them with these filenames.

Scope and limits

Live merge sorts each polling batch, not all future arrivals: late events stay appended. Initial contents are loaded into memory and the temporary merged file grows. Truncation is detected when size decreases; replacement with a same-size or larger file can miss events. The three columns are consecutive pages, not one column per service.

FLIK 0.2.0 · November 5, 2026

Inspect more formats and investigate structured events

Broader structured-log support and investigation tools reduce the manual preparation needed before inspecting cloud, web and system logs.

Flik 0.2.0: changes and practical benefits
FeatureWhat changedWhat it helps you do
Cloud, system and custom formatsAdds CloudWatch and Google Cloud Logging field handling, Logfmt detection, auth/syslog enrichment, extended access logs and named custom regex formats.Inspect fields from more existing log formats without first converting each file to a common schema.
Correlation and JSON inspectionAdds correlation identifier extraction, the J JSON inspector and nested JSON completion in search and filter editors.Locate identifiers and inspect nested payloads while refining an investigation.
Full-file analytics optionThe S dashboard can switch from its default sample to a full indexed-file scan with a. Live error-rate alerting is also available.Choose between a quick sampled overview and a broader count; keep the scope of the result explicit.
Configuration and distributionAdds global TOML configuration, modular format definitions, native Windows binaries and the Homebrew tap.Reuse settings and install a prebuilt binary on the supported platform.

Try it

flik --format logfmt app.log
flik /var/log/auth.log
Scope and limits

Field extraction depends on the input format. The default S dashboard remains sampled until a full scan is selected. Correlation identifiers help investigation but do not establish causality.

FLIK 0.1.0 · October 26, 2026

A local interactive workspace for log investigation

The initial release established interactive filtering, context and navigation for local files and piped streams.

Flik 0.1.0: changes and practical benefits
FeatureWhat changedWhat it helps you do
Indexed file navigationBackground byte-offset indexing supports direct navigation through local log files.Move through a file and refine the visible result while indexing progresses.
Filters and contextStack include/exclude conditions and use smart find to retain surrounding lines.Inspect the evidence around an error instead of retaining only matching lines.
Investigation workspaceIncludes independent split panes, time and frequency tools, request correlation workflows, incident export and session save/restore.Keep the investigation state and source context together while moving between questions.

Try it

flik app.log
flik api.log worker.log
Scope and limits

The byte-offset index still uses memory proportional to line count. Initial distribution covered Linux and macOS. This version does not include the continuously followed CLI multi-file merge or the three-column layout added in 0.3.0.

Update to the latest version

brew update
brew upgrade torxx666/tap/flik
flik --version

For a first Homebrew installation, use brew install torxx666/tap/flik. You can also download the matching archive and SHA256SUMS directly.
